verdict: Revision 2 fixes every prior consistency contradiction that was checked (genesis dek_gen >= 1; phase 1 now carries SubmitEpoch/epochflow; S2 accepts a two-key recovery; reencrypted is one definition with installed_digest; the v3 DDL is valid SQLite; Hello{have}; StageVersions open to any registered identity; MAX_VALUE and the three read bounds; RemoveIdentity carry-for-w-only; mode-E genesis in 7.2; S6 exempts recovery; rand_core 0.10; disclosure in crypto-design section 7; inline-built migration fixtures; all four TUI ACL keys) and every prior ambiguity (needs_rotation clears only on dek_gen+1, group_uid vs group_id, stage cap over retained ciphertext, idle TTL, service-admin column, SealedVersion provenance, --acl/--keep-acl, reset-pin, Ready=False/ChainRejected, C2->EpochConflict everywhere, src_dek_gen/src_nonce, per-i k hedge, byte budgets, step-8 rebase). Symbol audit against the tree: every Rust symbol, file, request variant and crate version the revision claims exists today does (to_scalar is not hazmat-gated in ed25519-dalek 3.0.0; iroh-base 1.0.3 has SecretKey::as_signing_key; curve25519-dalek 5.0.0 API and features as described; Store::audit is &self on the connection so audit_in is genuinely new; read_secret takes the age identity; ReplicaInner::age_identity, backfill_reader_wraps, Bunker::handle holding the lock across dispatch, touched_groups exhaustive, replica dispatch exhaustive, events.rs exhaustive match, SyncRequest::Hello unit, both wire_format_is_stable tests, MAX_MSG 4 MiB, exit 2 = VersionConflict, KeyRole filenames/is_age, db grant, recover, emptyDir mirror, README reason table, hkdf 0.12.4, subtle 2.6.1, sha2 0.10 / rand 0.8 pins). What the fixes introduced: the phase split now leaves the phase-1+2 release with no working orphan-group or operational-key-compromise path (db grant/recover are broken by v3 but their replacement is phase 3); the two-key operational replacement is described three incompatible ways (S2 'next', 6.4 'previous' + meta advanced later, section 8 meta key operational_ed25519_previous); G6's revival rule reads two ways and under the enforceable reading collides with 6.2's delta re-application and with S9; the freeze and the rate limit are silent about server-authored records; epoch log prints data the Epochs reply does not carry; revoked_identity/replica_revoked/revive guard a state the revised 6.3 makes unreachable; and several smaller section-vs-section mismatches (mode 'fixed at genesis', ReplicaInner::age_identity replaced while the transitional age read path is kept, group_pin 'replica and CLI' vs the JSON pin file). None of these changes the architecture; all are rule-text or phasing fixes, but a plan cannot be finalised on the two-key wording, the phase split or G6 as written. placeholders: Header 'Status: draft, awaiting user review (see section 19)'; section 19 lists 15 open questions whose answers 'change the spec'. Section 6.3 still defers a plan-affecting decision inline: '(Whether the Go client needs either is Q2.)' - whether additive legacy Grant/RotateDek must keep working for the Go client is unresolved.

Section 5 S8: 'Verified records and DEKs are cached in memory keyed by record hash (bounded LRU, zeroized on evict)' - no bound (entries or bytes) and no flag; section 11's serve flags do not add one.

Section 12 step 1: 'the operator removes the identity with `db remove-identity` or renames nothing - a longer name is refused with the list' - the middle clause is unreadable; no group-rename command exists in main.rs (DbCmd has Grant and AuditVerify only), so a database holding a >255-byte group name has no stated path to migration.

contradictions.where: Section 16 phase table (rows 1 and 3, lines 1220-1222) vs section 6.4 (line 728: 'This one flow replaces `db grant` (orphaned group) and `recover` (operational-key compromise)'), section 11 (line 1083: '`db grant` and `recover` are removed'), section 6.3 RemoveIdentity ('Never blocked; may orphan a group (G2 exception), whose recovery is 6.4'), section 7.4 ('Compromised operational key ... Replaced by per-group recoveries') and section 17 criterion 5.
contradictions.detail: Phase 1 ships schema v3, Ed25519 keys, server-authored RemoveIdentity carries (which may orphan a group) and 'Get/Put via the head record'; `recovery author`, `client epoch export|submit` and the removal of `db grant`/`recover` are phase 3, and the two-key `serve --previous-operational-key` of 6.4 appears in no phase row. On the phase-1+2 release the old tools no longer work: main.rs DbCmd::Grant (line 264) re-wraps by unwrapping `dek_wrap` rows with the age operational key and writes `group_acl` rows, but section 8 says `dek_wrap` is empty after migration and `group_acl` is a projection rebuilt from the head record inside every apply, so a `db grant` either fails (read bit: nothing to unwrap) or writes an unsigned ACL row that the next apply wipes and that every replica ignores (P5); `Recover` (main.rs:103) rewrites `dek_wrap` operational wraps that no longer exist and takes an age public key the v3 server does not use. Result: between the phase-1+2 release and phase 3 an orphaned group (a routine RemoveIdentity of a sole admin) and a suspected operational-key compromise have no recovery path at all, and section 17 criterion 5 is unreachable for that release - the same shape as the prior finding about additive grants, moved one phase later.
contradictions.resolution: Move `recovery author`, `client epoch export|submit` and the two-key `serve` into phase 1 (they are the only path 6.4 provides and RemoveIdentity ships in phase 1), leaving TUI polish and docs in phase 3; or state that `db grant`/`recover` are deleted in phase 1 and that until phase 3 an orphaned group is unrecoverable, and say so in 6.3/7.4/17.

contradictions.where: Section 5 S2 (line 540: 'the record's `authority` is the configured operational key or the configured *next* operational key (6.4)') vs section 6.4 'Operational-key replacement' (lines 736-745: '`serve --operational-key new.key --previous-operational-key old.key` holds both keys ... when none [names the old authority], `meta.operational_ed25519` is advanced (audited `authority-rotated`) and the old key is dropped at the next restart') vs section 8 meta list (line 901: `operational_ed25519, operational_ed25519_previous`) vs S2's genesis clause ('For `genesis`, `authority`/`backup`/`mode` equal the server's configured values') and A1/A3 (`author == authority`).
contradictions.detail: Three framings that do not compose. Under 6.4, mid-transition `meta.operational_ed25519` still holds the OLD key (it is 'advanced' only when no group names the old authority) while the primary `--operational-key` flag names the NEW key, so 'the configured operational key' in S2 is the old one and the 'next' one is the flag - but section 8's key name `operational_ed25519_previous` implies meta already holds the new key with the old one as previous, i.e. the opposite assignment; S2 calls the second key 'next', 6.4 and 8 call it 'previous'. Consequences a planner cannot resolve from the text: (a) which key a `CreateGroup` genesis is signed with and carries as `authority` during the window (S2 genesis rule says 'the server's configured values' - now two); (b) which key signs authority-authored carries/rotates for a group whose head still names the old key (A1/A3 require `author == authority` of the head, so it must be the old key, but 6.4 only says the wrap is 'opened' with whichever key the head names, not signed); (c) what `meta.operational_ed25519` is used for at all if `serve` is driven by flags; (d) whether `init`/`db migrate-epochs`, which 'record `operational_ed25519`', ever disagree with the flag at start.
contradictions.resolution: Define once: `meta.operational_ed25519` = the key `--operational-key` names, updated (audited `authority-rotated`) at `serve` start whenever the flag differs; `meta.operational_ed25519_previous` = the key `--previous-operational-key` names, cleared when the flag is dropped and refused if any head still names it. S2: for `recovery` the record's `authority` is either meta value; for `genesis` it is `operational_ed25519`. Server-authored records on a group are signed by, and open wraps with, the key the group's head names (A1/A3); genesis uses the current key. Replace 'next' in S2 with 'previous' and make 6.4 use the same two names as section 8.

contradictions.where: Section 5 G6 (lines 520-525, applies to `rewrap` only, 'enforced by every verifier by comparing the ACL to `head.acl`') vs section 6.2 EpochConflict rule (line 665: 're-apply the *delta* (add carol; clear bits on X) to the new head') and 6.2 last sentence ('G6 is the server-side backstop'), and vs S9 (one accepted non-rotating record per author per group per 30 s).
contradictions.detail: A verifier that compares only to `head.acl` cannot tell a kicked id from a never-seen id, so the enforceable rule is: a `rewrap` that adds any id absent from `head.acl` must change nothing else. Then 6.2's own conflict recipe - one record that adds carol AND clears bits on X - is refused by G6 whenever carol is not already in `head.acl` (the normal case), and adding N readers needs N records which S9 spaces 30 s apart (a three-reader grant takes over a minute and three signatures). 6.2 also calls G6 'the server-side backstop' while G6 is a verifier rule for server, replica and client (section 18 ticks all three). Conversely, G6 constrains `rewrap` only: a `rotate` whose ACL both kicks bob and adds a previously-kicked carol, or a `carry` that re-adds a previously-kicked id as write-only, is not covered, so the 'not by accident' intent is enforced on exactly one of the three kinds that can add an id.
contradictions.resolution: Pick one reading and state it for every non-authority kind: either (a) 'a record whose ACL contains ids absent from `head.acl` MUST change nothing else in the ACL' (rewrap, rotate and carry alike; then rewrite 6.2's delta rule as 'one record per added id, then one record for bit changes' and note the S9 spacing), or (b) scope G6 to ids that appear in an earlier record of the chain (server and replica hold the chain; clients with only a pin skip G6 and say so in section 18), which leaves multi-change rewraps legal for brand-new ids. Drop 'server-side backstop' from 6.2.

contradictions.where: Section 6.5 log format (lines 757-759: '#12 ... re-encrypted 143 by alice + 2 by the server' and '#10 ... authority (requested by carol, unsigned)') and the paragraph after it ('Authority-authored records are rendered with the audit requester marked as unsigned') vs section 9 `GroupEpochs` reply (line 938: `Epochs{records: [bstr], head_epoch: uint, names: [...]}`) and `Status.last_rotate {epoch, author, at, staged, by_server}`.
contradictions.detail: The per-record straggler split ('143 by alice + 2 by the server') lives in `group_epoch.installed_digest` and the audit row (4.3); the wire requester of an authority record lives only in the audit row (6.3: 'the audit row names the wire requester'). `Epochs` carries opaque records, `head_epoch` and a names map - neither datum - and `Status.last_rotate` carries counts for the newest rotate only. `client epoch log` as specified therefore cannot print lines #10 or #12 from any request in section 9; the audit log is not readable over the wire.
contradictions.resolution: Either add a server-attested per-record side table to `Epochs` (e.g. `meta: [{epoch: uint, requested_by: text or null, staged: uint, by_server: uint}]`, explicitly unsigned) and mention it in 4.3/6.5/9 and the golden vectors, or cut the requester and straggler split from the `epoch log` line and keep them in `GroupStatus`/the audit log only.

contradictions.where: Section 6.3 RemoveIdentity (line 693: '`revoked_identity` records any id removed from the registry that still appears in a head ACL (mode E, until the rotate; or a race the S2 re-check lost)') vs 6.3 'Server-side revocation' (lines 676-683: under the lock, in one transaction, an authority `carry` per affected group 'that drops the identity's row' - both modes) vs S2 (line 536: re-checked 'inside the install transaction') and 6.1 server step 3 (S2 re-check under the lock in the same transaction as the install).
contradictions.detail: After the revised 6.3, a RemoveIdentity leaves no head ACL containing the id in either mode: the carry drops the row immediately (the mode-E 'until the rotate' clause describes the pre-revision design in which mode E had no carry), and the S2 re-check runs inside the install transaction under the same store mutex that serialises RemoveIdentity, so 'a race the S2 re-check lost' cannot occur. The `revoked_identity` table (8), the sync `revoked` list (10), `replica_revoked` and P5's subtraction, the deletion trigger 'when no head contains the id', and S7's `revive: true` ('an id that still appears in any group's head ACL') all describe a state with no population path; section 13 nevertheless tests 'S7 revive'.
contradictions.resolution: Either delete `revoked_identity`, `replica_revoked`, the `revoked` sync field, P5's subtraction and `AddIdentity.revive` (S7 then reads 'AddIdentity refuses an id that appears in any head ACL'), or keep them as declared defence-in-depth and rewrite the 6.3 sentence to name the only way the state can arise (an authoritative restore from a snapshot taken between the registry delete and the carry, or a future mode-E without server carries) and make S7's revive text match.

contradictions.where: Section 4.1 layout (line 364: '`mode` u8 ... fixed at genesis') vs C4 ('`authority`, `backup` and `mode` equal the head's unless `kind = recovery`'), G4 ('`mode` immutable except by `recovery`'), the kinds table (`recovery`: 'mode change') and 6.4 (`--mode A|E`; trigger 'mode change').
contradictions.detail: The layout comment says `mode` is fixed at genesis; four other places make it changeable by a recovery record. A parser/verifier written from 4.1 would reject the mode-switch recovery 6.4 specifies (the same comment is correct for `name`, which every rule keeps immutable).
contradictions.resolution: Change the 4.1 comment to 'set at genesis; changed only by `recovery` (C4/G4)'.

contradictions.where: Section 12 step 3 (line 1119: '`ReplicaInner::age_identity` becomes the replica's Ed25519 scalar') vs section 10 'Transitional read path' (line 1034: 'A v3 replica keeps the age read path (`agebridge` + local `dek_wrap` rows) for a group that has no `group_epoch` rows yet') and section 8 ('The table and `agebridge.rs` are dropped in a later v4 cleanup').
contradictions.detail: The transitional read path needs the age identity (`Replica::get` at replica.rs:182 calls `crypto::unwrap_dek(&wrapped, &self.inner.age_identity)`; `server::read_secret` takes `&age::x25519::Identity`), so replacing the field removes the path section 10 relies on for 'a standalone replica serves its last mirror across the upgrade' and e2e test (5).
contradictions.resolution: 12.3: '`ReplicaInner` gains the Ed25519 scalar alongside `age_identity`; `age_identity` and `agebridge` go in v4'.

contradictions.where: Section 8 (line 889: `CREATE TABLE group_pin ( -- replica and CLI: survives dropping the group`) vs section 11 (line 1058: the CLI keeps a 'client pin file' `$XDG_DATA_HOME/secret-bunker-iroh/pins/<server EndpointId>.json`) and section 18 ('C1-C4 ... Client / auditor: ✓ (pin file)').
contradictions.detail: The CLI has no SQLite database; its pins are a JSON file per server. Section 8's comment assigns `group_pin` to the CLI as well, so a planner reading section 8 builds the client pin store in SQLite and one reading section 11 builds it as JSON keyed by server EndpointId (which `group_pin` does not key on).
contradictions.resolution: Section 8 comment: 'replica only'; section 11 stays the CLI's store.

contradictions.where: Section 4.3 (line 422: 'An offline auditor recomputes `reencrypted` from an export only when no stragglers were recorded') vs the same section's definition ('exactly as received by the server (including rows for versions deleted meanwhile)') and S4 ('Rows staged for a version that no longer exists ... are not installed').
contradictions.detail: Rows for versions deleted during the window are in the signed digest but not in any later export, so recomputation also fails after a delete during the window, not only after stragglers; 4.3's own two sentences disagree on the precondition.
contradictions.resolution: '... only when no stragglers were recorded and no staged row was dropped at install (both counts are in the audit row and `GroupStatus.last_rotate`)'; add a `dropped: uint` to `last_rotate` if the auditor is meant to know.

ambiguities.where: Section 5 S10 (lines 579-584: while frozen 'every non-`recovery` `SubmitEpoch`, every legacy `Grant` and every `Put`' are refused) vs section 6.3 (RemoveIdentity 'Never blocked', authors a carry per affected group and, in mode A, a rotate 'retried with backoff until it lands') and 6.4 step 0-1 (freeze, then export the bundle the offline recovery chains on, C2).
ambiguities.detail: Reading 1: server-authored records are not SubmitEpochs and land on a frozen group; then a RemoveIdentity during the freeze (the natural first response to a rogue admin, or any unrelated removal of an identity with a row on the group) moves the head, the hours-old bundle fails C2 with EpochConflict, and the ceremony restarts - the exact failure the freeze was added to prevent. Reading 2: the freeze also holds server-authored records; then 'always wins' and 'never blocked' are false for frozen groups and the rotating half's retry loop spins against the freeze.
ambiguities.resolution: State it: the carry half lands on a frozen group (denial-of-a-removed-key is the freeze's own purpose) and the rotating half is deferred until the freeze clears; 6.4 step 1 notes that a RemoveIdentity touching the group after the export requires re-export, and `client epoch submit` prints the intervening records on EpochConflict as 6.1 step 8 does.

ambiguities.where: Section 5 S9 ('at most one accepted non-rotating record per author per group per 30 s') vs section 6.3 ('All server-authored records go through the same verifier and the same two-phase discipline'; RemoveIdentity 'Never blocked') and A4/6.4 (recovery).
ambiguities.detail: Reading 1: S9 applies to every author including `authority` and `backup` - then two RemoveIdentity calls within 30 s that both touch the same group (bulk offboarding, or a legacy shrink Grant followed by a removal) have the second authority carry refused, contradicting 'always wins', and a corrected recovery re-submitted within 30 s of a rejected one is refused. Reading 2: S9 applies to wire `SubmitEpoch` by non-authority authors only - then S9's stated purpose (churn by an online admin) holds and the server path is unaffected, but the text does not say so.
ambiguities.resolution: Scope S9 to `SubmitEpoch` records whose `author` is neither `authority` nor `head.backup`; say so in S9 and in the 'Server-only' preamble.

ambiguities.where: Section 6.3 legacy `Grant` (line 697: 'A pure shrink (bits cleared, `perms = 0`) performs the server-side revocation ... Any addition or raised bit answers `Failed`') vs section 11 TUI ('a service admin without an explicit row is offered the server-side revocation (legacy shrink `Grant`) for `x`/`r`-off'), 6.1 step 8 ('legacy Grant with the read bit cleared') and D13 ('legacy read revocations').
ambiguities.detail: Reading 1: only `perms = 0` is a shrink; a request lowering rwa->w (read cleared, write kept) is neither 'perms = 0' nor 'addition or raised bit' and has no specified reply, while section 11 and 6.1 rely on exactly that request. Reading 2: any strict subset of the current bits is a shrink; then '`perms = 0`' in the parenthetical is a stray example.
ambiguities.resolution: 'A request whose bits are a strict subset of the current row's (including `perms = 0`) performs the server-side revocation: a carry, plus the rotate when the read bit was cleared; a request that is neither a subset nor equal answers `Failed{...}`.'

ambiguities.where: Section 6.2 bullet 1 ('Add reader / change bits touching no reader ... `rewrap`') vs bullet 2 ('w/a-only edits (recipients unchanged): `carry`'), the kinds table (`rewrap`: 'ACL edits that touch no reader'; `carry`: 'w/a-bit edits') and section 11 TUI ('`r`-on and `a`-on -> `rewrap`; `w` either way and `a`-off -> `carry`').
ambiguities.detail: A write-bit change on a non-reader 'touches no reader' (bullet 1: rewrap) and is a 'w/a-only edit with recipients unchanged' (bullet 2: carry). Raising `a` on an entry that already has `r` leaves recipients unchanged (bullet 2: carry) but section 11 sends a `rewrap`. The two kinds have different costs (rewrap: n ElGamal wraps and a proof; carry: none), different S6 treatment and different golden vectors, so the CLI/TUI code paths differ by which sentence the implementer reads.
ambiguities.resolution: One rule everywhere: recipients enlarged -> `rewrap`; recipients unchanged -> `carry`; a `rewrap` with unchanged recipients is only the explicit repair (`client epoch repair`). Fix the kinds-table cell to 'add a reader; repair a bad head' and section 11 to '`r`-on, or `a`-on on an entry without `r` -> rewrap; `a`-on on a reader, `w` either way, `a`-off -> carry'.

ambiguities.where: Section 10 `Hello{have: [{group, have_epoch, have_hash}]}` and 'the whole chain for a name it did not list' vs P1/P3 (a replica revoked under P3 drops the mirror but keeps `group_pin`) and R4/R5/R2 (which need head.wraps, the seen-c0 set 'per group it mirrors' and every commit seen).
ambiguities.detail: After P3 the replica holds only the pin (hashes and epoch numbers), not the records. Reading 1: it lists the group with the pinned `head_epoch`; the server ships only later records and the replica cannot run R4 (no head wraps), R5 (seen set gone) or R2. Reading 2: it omits the group (or sends `have_epoch: 0`), receives the whole chain, and must check that it passes through both the pinned `genesis_hash` (C1) and the pinned `(head_epoch, head_hash)` (P1) - which P1 words as 'chain does not pass through the pinned head' without saying the replica may be behind the pin's own head.
ambiguities.resolution: P1/P3: a pin-only group is listed with `have_epoch: 0`; the received chain must contain the pinned genesis at epoch 1 and the pinned `head_hash` at `head_epoch`, and the seen-c0/seen-commit sets are rebuilt from it before the newer records are verified.

ambiguities.where: Section 5 R2 ('`rotate`: `dek_commit` differs from **every** commit seen in the chain') vs R5's last sentence ('a client that holds only a pin enforces them over the records it fetched') and section 18 ('R1-R6 ... Client / auditor: ✓ (R5 over fetched records)').
ambiguities.detail: R5 states the reduced scope for a pin-only client; R2's 'every commit seen in the chain' has no such clause, and section 18 names only R5 as relaxed. Reading 1: the client must fetch from genesis to apply R2 (then 6.1 step 1's `since: pinned head` is insufficient). Reading 2: R2 is also evaluated over fetched records only.
ambiguities.resolution: Add to R2 the same 'over the records it fetched' clause for a pin-only client, and cite both in section 18.

ambiguities.where: Section 10 P1 ('The rejection clears, with `ReplicaEvent::ChainAccepted{group}`, when a head for the group is accepted') vs the operator paragraph ('the operator persists `group_pin` rows in an operator-owned Secret ... written on every accepted head').
ambiguities.detail: Reading 1: `ChainAccepted` fires only on the transition out of a rejection; then the operator has no event for the ordinary case (every accepted head) and no accessor to read pin rows (`SyncStatus` gains `rejected`, not pins; `ReplicaBuilder::pins(...)` is input only), so 'written on every accepted head' has no data path - the same shape as the prior `ChainRejected` finding. Reading 2: it fires on every accepted head, which makes the P1 sentence misleading and the operator's k8s Event/log noisy.
ambiguities.resolution: Add `ReplicaEvent::HeadAccepted{group, epoch, hash}` (every accepted head, data event after commit) and `Replica::pins() -> Vec<GroupPin>`; keep `ChainAccepted` as the transition event; the operator writes the pins Secret on `HeadAccepted`.

missing_for_planning: The entry point for S8's lock/release/blocking-thread/lock sequence: `Bunker::handle` (server.rs:197) is synchronous and holds the store mutex across `dispatch`, and `accept` (server.rs:1019-1021) calls `handle_raw` inline; the spec never says whether `handle` becomes async, whether `SubmitEpoch` (and the rotating half of RemoveIdentity/legacy Grant) get their own path in `accept`, or where the background retry task of 6.3 lives and how it publishes `Changed` (today `inner.events.send` happens inside `handle`). Also `handle` appends an audit row `(req.op(), req.target(), outcome)` after dispatch while 6.1 step 3 writes a `submit-epoch` row via `audit_in` inside the transaction: two `submit-epoch` rows per request unless `handle` is changed.

Uniform denial for the other new requests: S1 fixes the oracle for `SubmitEpoch` only. `StageVersions{group: X}` is open to any registered identity and answers `Ok` - the reply for an unknown `X`, a group the caller holds no row on, a frozen group, or a byte-cap overflow is unspecified (`Failed` vs `Ok` distinguishes existence); likewise `FreezeGroup` on an unknown group and `GroupStatus`/`GroupEpochs` for non-readers on replicas. Section 13 tests the oracle for `SubmitEpoch` alone.

How the operator invokes `Replica::reset_group(group, expected_genesis)` and `Replica::pins()` (no flag, HTTP endpoint or CRD field is named; with pins in the `<release>-bunker-pins` Secret, is a reset an edit of that Secret?), and the chart/flag for `--tofu`: P2 rejects genesis without configuration, pin or `--tofu`, section 12.4 says replicas 'resync from genesis and pin it (seeded by `bunker.expect*`)', but no `bunker.tofu` value or default is given, so a chart upgrade with unset `expect*` values rejects every group.

Which kind and which key a server-authored record uses on a group whose head names the previous operational key during the two-key window (see the S2/6.4/8 contradiction), and what `db migrate-epochs`/`init` write to `meta.operational_ed25519` when `serve` is later started with a different `--operational-key`.

The stage lifecycle for server-authored rotates: 6.1 says the two-phase discipline covers 'server-authored rotates' and step 3 'delete[s] the stage', but 6.3's rotating half re-encrypts every retained version itself - whether those rows pass through `epoch_stage` (submitter = authority?) or stay in memory, and what happens to a client stage open on the same group when the authority rotate lands (the client's rows are under the old source generation and now fail S4 by `src_dek_gen`), is unstated; 13's Store tests ('stage keys, cap, idle TTL, replacement') do not cover it.

`ReplicaEvent::ChainAccepted`'s exact firing rule and a per-record straggler/requester source for `epoch log` (see contradictions) - both needed before the operator (`events.rs`, `reconcile.rs`) and `epochflow` can be planned.
